correctness.rationale: Iterated Schwarz lemma yields |conjugate(z) f(z)|<=|z|^(m+1); the Möbius image is an explicit disk. AM–GM bounds each disk radius by the exact convex interpolation radius. For \(f(z)=z^m\) every fixed-radius boundary circle is traversed and its circles tend to the extremal outer circle, proving equality of closed convex hulls and every support direction. Tangency and major-arc integration give exact area and perimeter; a monomial-basis decomposition checks the auxiliary ordinary numerical-range assertion. The extracted standalone checker passed 2,002 supplementary assertions, which are finite tests and not the universal proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The prior scalar bound \(|\mathcal B_f(z)|\le1\) for any fixed-point symbol is weaker: its unit-disk target has area pi, versus the optimal convex envelope with area asymptotic to 1/m. Known circle-fiber coverage for a special class does not imply universal containment for all f with vanishing order m. The standard Schwarz lemma is an ingredient rather than a theorem about the quotient image.

value.rationale: The sharp all-directions complex bound resolves a natural geometric optimization problem for normalized evaluation kernels under a finite jet constraint, giving an explicit universal extremizer and two-tangent convex body for each higher order m. The exact shape/area/perimeter and inverse-degree concentration quantify a large gap relative to the coarse radius-one estimate and the unchanging full numerical range. The target is natural (all symbols with order-m zero) and not a selected arbitrary slice. No generalization to arbitrary weighted kernels or individual nonconvex symbols is asserted.
